predecessors.note: The Attica page: the communities 'were progressively incorporated into an Athenian state during the 8th and the 7th centuries BC'. -700 is the boundary of the two centuries, not a dated founding.

land.text: Attica under Antipater's regency: 'Antipater dissolved the Athenian government and established a plutocratic system in 322 BC'; Macedonian garrison at Munychia

successors.note: Athens remained a polis (infobox 'Hellenistic Athens 322 BC-86 BC') but 'ceased to be an independent power'; the Hellenistic and Roman-era Athens is outside this batch's scope (Alexander's death) and belongs to a later extension. Cliopatria's Macedonian Empire shape of 323-319 has no Attica of its own; eu-01-b keeps Attica in the Greek City-States aggregate.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Athenian row; Attica is drawn inside the Greek City-States aggregate (-800..-378), the Delian League (-478..-404) and the Second Athenian League (-378..-338, Attica direct), and is missing from Cliopatria in -337..-324 (eu-01-b). No page gives an area for Attica (the Attica page has only 'the 10 mi (16 km) long Cithaeron and Parnes mountain ranges'), so the infobox comparison could not be made; the gazetteer's Attica is 3,288 km2. The overseas cleruchies of Athens (Lemnos, Imbros, Chalcis, the Thracian Chersonese, Lesbos 'the 3,000 kleroi on Lesbos') are not drawn because no page opened dates them; the Delian League allies are in delian-league.

correction.text: Attica plus the Athenian colony on Samos kept after Chaeronea

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Attica plus the Athenian colony on Samos. 'Although the Second Athenian League was dissolved, the Athenians were allowed to keep their colony on Samos' (Chaeronea, 338); the Lamian War page shows Perdiccas demanding that Athens 'evacuate Samos' in 322. The Cleruchy page says cleruchies were 're-established in the fourth century, for example at Lemnos and Samos' but gives no year; the Lamian War page dates it: 'the island of Samos, colonised by Athenian clerurchs since 365 BC' (reviewer eu-01-x, 2026-10-18: was -350 bridged). The colony is held 365-322. Lemnos is not drawn (no date).

region.text: Attica, the peninsula of the Athenian polis (the gazetteer's Attica, 3,288 km2)

ledger.note: ~700: Athens, the Attic state. 'the communities were progressively incorporated into an Athenian state during the 8th and the 7th centuries BC'; the traditional account puts it 'during the reign of Theseus'. The page names no year; -700 is the boundary between the two centuries.

6th century: Athens takes Salamis from Megara. 'The first cleruchy is thought to have been Salamis, captured by Athens from Megara in the 6th century BC.' The page gives the century only; -600 is a bridging date. The island is already inside the gazetteer's Attica, so the drawn shape does not change (about 95 km2).

region.text: Attica, the peninsula of the Athenian polis (the gazetteer's Attica, 3,288 km2)

ledger.note: 508: Cleisthenes establishes Athenian democracy. Infobox 'Cleisthenes establishes Athenian democracy: 508 BC'. The Attica page: 'Only after Peisistratos's tyranny and the reforms implemented by Cleisthenes did the local communities lose their independence', i.e. Attica is fully one polis from here; the page gives no year for that step.

365: Athenian cleruchs settle Samos. Lamian War page: Athens 'had to surrender the island of Samos, colonised by Athenian clerurchs since 365 BC'; the Cleruchy page: cleruchies 're-established in the fourth century, for example at Lemnos and Samos'; the Chaeronea page shows the colony held in 338 and the Lamian War page shows it still held in 322. (Reviewer eu-01-x, 2026-10-18: year corrected from the bridged -350.)

322: Athens loses Oropos and Samos. 'Athens lost the city of Oropus and the sanctuary of the Amphiareion' on its northern border; Perdiccas 'demanded Athens to evacuate Samos'; Athens had to 'lose its possessions outside Attica'.

region.text: Attica, the peninsula of the Athenian polis (the gazetteer's Attica, 3,288 km2)

ledger.note: 322 (September): the Athenian democracy ends. Lamian War page: the Macedonian garrison at Munychia was 'taken on 18 September 322 BC'; only citizens with more than 2,000 drachmas kept their rights (21,000 reduced to 9,000). Classical Athens page: 'Antipater dissolved the Athenian government and established a plutocratic system in 322 BC'; Athens 'ceased to be an independent power'.

wars.name: Peloponnesian War
wars.outcome: 'The war ended with the complete defeat of Athens in 404'; the Delian League was dissolved under Lysander.
wars.note: The pages opened give no territorial zone inside Attica; the 404 loss of the empire and its cleruchies ('This network of cleruchies was lost at the end of the Peloponnesian War', Cleruchy page) is not a ledger event because no cleruchy is drawn (no Decelea or Spartan invasion); delian-league and peloponnesian-league carry the contest and occupation events.

wars.name: Social War (357-355 BC)
wars.outcome: 'This war ended in the disintegration of the Second Athenian League'; 'most of the allied cities became independent'.
wars.note: Allies' land is in second-athenian-league; Athens' own Attica is unchanged.

wars.name: Battle of Chaeronea
wars.outcome: Philip II 'treated Athens very leniently': the league was dissolved, Athens kept its Samos colony, prisoners were released without ransom.
wars.note: A battle, listed for the League of Corinth settlement that followed (Athens a member, Macedonian garrisons only at Thebes, Corinth and Chalcis).

wars.outcome: Macedonian victory: garrison at Munychia on 18 September 322, oligarchy of 9,000, Oropos and Samos lost, navy given up.
wars.note: The page's territorial list is Oropos and Samos; the infobox gives no territorial changes.

certainty.note: The Attic frontier follows the Cithaeron and Parnes ranges to the north (Attica page) and the sea elsewhere, but no treaty line is dated; overseas holdings (Samos, cleruchies) are islands and points, not frontiers.

notes: Athens is written here as the Attic polis itself (Attica plus the colony on Samos), 700-322. Overlaps the orchestrator must settle: Attica is already inside Cliopatria's Greek City-States (-800..-378, eu-01-b), the Delian League (-478..-404, with Athens as capital), the Second Athenian League (-378..-338, written by eu-01-c as 'Attica direct, allies as client tint') and Cliopatria has no Attica in -337..-324 (eu-01-b fills it). The cleanest rendering is Attica as 'athens' throughout and the two leagues as the allies only; this dossier does not edit those. The pages opened (all Wikipedia, and thin on territory) give no date for Athens' cleruchies on Lemnos, Imbros, Chalcis, the Thracian Chersonese, Lesbos or Aegina, none for Oropos before 322, and no area for Attica; they are therefore not drawn, and a gap-filler should open 'Oropos', 'Lemnos', 'Chalcis' and 'Thirty Years' Peace'. The state continues after 322 ('Hellenistic Athens 322 BC-86 BC', Cassander 316, Sulla 88-85, free city under Rome) outside this batch's scope; eu-01-b already asked for a free-city 'athens' dossier from -86. Gazetteer names used that it lacks: Salamis (place), Samos (place), Oropos (place). The Salamis event at -600 and the Samos colony at -350 are bridging dates (confidence 1); the -700 start is the page's span (8th and 7th centuries). Sparta, the other state this batch was asked to add, is already written by eu-01-c as 'peloponnesian-league' (name 'Sparta (Peloponnesian League)', -800..-192) and was not duplicated.
